storedTranscript.text: Hello, I'm Ryota, and welcome to your English lesson! Today we'll talk about your work and a recent project, using the present perfect for your experience and the past simple for finished events. We'll start with a short, friendly conversation so I can see your level. Does that sound good to you?
Yes.

Great, let's begin. This is a short, friendly chat so I can see what you already can do. Please answer in English, and don't worry about mistakes.

Can you tell me a little about your job? What do you do?
I, I work as admin at the company.
Admin work keeps an office running well. What kind of admin tasks do you do most days?
I'm checking emails. and sorting out some paperwork.
That sounds like a busy and important job. Have you ever worked with an international customer? If so, can you tell me about the experience?
Please, could you please rephrase that, please?
Of course. Simpler: have you ever worked with a customer from another country?
Yes, I have.
Thank you. Can you tell me about that experience? What did you do with that customer?
How to communicate with the non in not the Japanese people with not the with people with the in and not from Japan.
Sorry, I didn't catch that. Did you ask how to communicate with people who are not from Japan? Please tell me in a few words.
Could you explain that in Japanese?

海外のお客様と仕事をしたことがあるか、という質問です。あった場合は、その経験について少し話してください。

Please try to answer in English. You can start with: "Yes, I have worked with…"

Does that make sense?
I want uh improve my speaking skill because I often attend a meeting.
that use English.
Of course, I'll use English only. Please just tell me one thing: have you worked with a customer from another country?
Yes, I have.
Thank you. What was it like working with that customer? Please tell me a little about it.
Uh, what do you mean?
Sorry, that was unclear. Please tell me one thing you did with that customer. For example, did you send emails, have meetings, or answer questions?
I do emails and sorting out some documents.

Thank you, that's clear. Today we'll make your sentences more accurate and natural, starting with talking about your job.

Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
Yes.

では、仕事について話す練習をしましょう。まず、簡単な文から始めます。

Now it's your turn. Please say one sentence about your job, starting with "I work in…".

I joined my company three years ago.
I do accounting and some admin work.

That's a clear sentence. Accounting and admin work are good skills to have in an office.

How long have you worked at your company? Please say a number of years.
I have worked for the current company for 10 years.

Yes, that's right. You used "have worked" because you started in the past and you still work there now.

This part is done. Next is the present perfect, which we use for experience that started in the past and continues now. Shall we go on?
Yes.

現在完了は、過去に始まって今も続いている経験に使います。形は have か has に過去分詞を付けます。

Now it's your turn. Please say one sentence starting with "I have worked…", about your company.

I have worked with customers from other countries.
I have worked for my current company for 10 years.

Yes, that's right. You used "have worked" for something that started in the past and continues now.

This part is done. Next is the past simple, which we use for finished events at a specific time, like "last year." Shall we go on?
Yes.

過去の終わった出来事には過去形を使います。「last year」や「in 2022」のような、いつかがはっきりしている時に使います。

Now it's your turn. Please say one sentence about something you did last year, using a past verb.

I attended an exhibition last year.
I finished accounting yesterday.

Good, "I finished accounting yesterday" is correct. "Yesterday" is a specific time, so we use the past simple "finished."

Where did you study accounting? Please answer with one sentence that starts with "I studied…".
I don't really know.

That's fine, no problem. Let's make it easier: you can just say a school or university name, or "I don't remember." Or try this, in English: "I studied at…"

Which one feels closer to your answer?
Could you repeat that, please?
Sure. Please say this sentence: "I studied at…" and then the name of the school or university, or just say "I studied at" and stop.
Could you repeat that? please?

「I studied at」のあとに、学校の名前を言ってください。たとえば「I studied at Nagoya University.」です。

Please say: I studied at… and then the school name.

Does that make sense?
Yes.
OK. Please say your own sentence now, starting with "I studied at…". You can use the name of any school or university.
Please move on to the past. simple.

わかりました、学校の質問はここで終わりにします。次は、去年の出来事を使って過去形を練習しましょう。

Please answer in English.

Did you attend any business events or exhibitions last year? Answer with one sentence, starting with "I attended…" or "I didn't attend…".
No.
Thank you. Please say a full sentence, starting with "I didn't attend…".
No, I didn't.

「No, I didn't.」は正しい過去形の否定です。「didn't」の後ろは動詞の原形を使います。

Now please say the full sentence: "I didn't attend any exhibitions last year."

Does that make sense so far?
Yes.

では、その文を英語で言ってみましょう。「I didn't attend any exhibitions last year.」です。

Does that make sense?
Yes.
Please say the full sentence now: "I didn't attend any exhibitions last year."
No. I didn't.

「No, I didn't.」で大丈夫です。次は「didn't」のあとに「attend」を続けます。

Now please say that full sentence once.

I didn't attend any exhibitions last year.

Are you with me so far?
No, I have not.

「No, I have not.」は、「last year」という過去の特定の時間には合いません。過去形の「No, I didn't.」を使いましょう。

Please say that full sentence once.

Does that make sense so far?
Yes.
Good. Now say the whole sentence once: "I didn't attend any exhibitions last year."
What do you mean by 'important project'?

An important project is a piece of work that matters a lot to your company or to you, for example a big task that took a long time. 大切な仕事、という意味です。

Did that answer your question?
Yes.
Good. Now let's go back to the sentence. Please say it once: "I didn't attend any exhibitions last year."
No, I have not.

Let's make it smaller. Please say just this part: "I didn't attend."

「I didn't attend.」だけ言ってみてください。

ゆっくりで大丈夫です。まず私が言います。 "I didn't attend."

Now you say it: "I didn't attend."

Are you with me so far?
No, I have not.

「No, I have not.」は、去年の特定の時間には使いません。正しい文はこれです。「No, I didn't attend any exhibitions last year.」「have not」ではなく「didn't」を使います。

This part is done. Next is a short conversation about your work. Shall we go on?
Yes.

では、仕事の話を少ししましょう。

Please answer in English. Try: "I worked on a project to…"
Could you give me some more example of past simple?

Yes, here are a few more. Listen, then try one about yourself.

Now say one sentence about something you did last week, starting with "I".

I joined my company three years ago.
The year and tax. system comparison.
Sorry, I didn't understand that. Did you want to say something about the sentence, or about the project question? Please tell me in a few words.
Because we implemented a new system for tax system this year and I was successfully finished all the new taxes on time.

Thank you, that's a real project, and "we implemented" is correct. One change: you said "I was successfully finished." We say "I successfully finished."

Please say that sentence once.

Does that make sense?
I successfully finished the new tasks because we implemented a new tax system this year.

Yes, that's right. "I successfully finished the new tasks" is clear and correct.

What was the hardest part of that project?
that that everything was new, that we didn't know them we we didn't have a manual to follow on.

Everything was new, and there was no manual to guide you. That is a strong point. One small change: we say "to follow," not "to follow on."

Please say that sentence once.

Does that make sense?
that I think successfully finished the new tasks because we implement the new system for tax. year in tax system.

You said "we implement," but this happened this year, so we need the past form: "we implemented." Please say the whole sentence once more.

Is that clear, or shall I go over it again?
I don't really remember, but maybe helps from or accounting office staff.

Thank you for that. You can say it this way: "We got help from the accounting office staff."

Today you talked about your work, your accounting duties and a tax project. We practised two grammar points.

Well done today. Your sentences about your company were clear. We didn't reach the pronunciation practice, so that's for next time. Keep using these two grammar points when you talk about your work. See you next time!
